report.source_text: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) was administered at 1 g/kg of body weight of the child. She was also started on oral prednisolone (2 mg/kg/day) which was later increased to 4 mg/kg/day. However, there was no response as the platelet count remained below <10 000/mm3 with new petechiae appearing along with oral mucosal bleed. She, again, underwent platelet transfusion. In addition, to ongoing steroid, she was started on thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor agonist. A single dose of inj. romiplostim was given once (1 μg/kg) and tab. eltrombopag (25 mg/day) was also started.

report.source_text: Five days into her maintenance therapy, she started to develop high-grade fever with cold and coryza. RT-PCR of the oropharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2. In view of this, her chemotherapy was immediately withheld and she was managed symptomatically. Her symptoms subsided over the next 5 days. Routine blood examination was within normal limits at the time. She was planned to be restarted on maintenance chemotherapy after 14 days of recovery from COVID-19.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) secondary to SARS-CoV-2 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 5.5-year-old girl with B-cell ALL (diagnosed 18 weeks prior, completed induction and consolidation phases, on maintenance therapy) developed SARS-CoV-2 infection with fever, coryza, and positive RT-PCR. Her symptoms resolved within 5 days with normal blood counts at that time. Chemotherapy was withheld and restarted after 14 days of recovery. Twenty-two days after SARS-CoV-2 recovery, she presented with reddish-purple petechiae and purpura on neck, shoulder, arms, and legs without other bleeding manifestations. Physical examination confirmed non-blanching spots consistent with thrombocytopenia. CBC revealed severe thrombocytopenia (3000/mm³) with normal hemoglobin (119 g/L), normal WBC (5.85×10⁹/L), and no blast cells on peripheral smear. Bone marrow aspiration showed normocellular marrow with increased megakaryopoiesis and no blast cells, confirming remission of B-cell ALL and ruling out leukemic relapse. Coagulation studies (PT, aPTT, INR) were normal with slightly elevated fibrinogen (411 mg/dL), ruling out DIC. Initial treatment with IVIg (1 g/kg) and prednisolone (2-4 mg/kg/day) failed, with platelet count remaining <10,000/mm³ and new oral mucosal bleeding. TPO receptor agonists (romiplostim 1 μg/kg and eltrombopag 25 mg/day) were initiated. Two weeks after TPO agonist therapy, platelet count improved to 24,000/mm³, and on subsequent investigations, platelets recovered to 157,000/mm³, confirming diagnosis and treatment response of ITP secondary to SARS-CoV-2.
